For the person who wants to be specific before they are ready to talk to anyone. You end up with a summary you can copy, circulate internally, or send to us — and if you send it, the conversation starts two steps further
Every answer stays in your browser. There is no submit until the end and no field asking who you are.

If you send it, it arrives as an enquiry with the answers attached, and the scope that comes back is more specific because of it. If you do not, nothing has happened — no cookie, no record, no follow-up.
Five lines of email works just as well. "We are forty people selling building materials and our stock numbers are never right" is a perfectly good brief.

An enquiry lands, gets an owner in seconds, and carries a coloured edge the moment its follow-up is due. Nothing sits unclaimed over a weekend, which is the single most expensive thing that happens in a small sales team.

e.h: Then it has to be deliverable
e.t: Available is on hand minus what is already promised — the only figure safe to quote against. Late orders are counted in rupees rather than in count, because six small ones are not the same meeting as one large one.

e.h: What the money side looks like
e.t: The dashboard you open to, the tax screens nobody enjoys, and the statements that are derived from the ledger rather than rebuilt from it every month.

e.h: And then it has to be collected
e.t: Ageing computed once and rendered everywhere, so the number on the screen is the number in the export. And input tax credit matched line by line against what your suppliers actually filed, with the money at risk named.

e.h: See it against your own data.
e.t: Where it is useful we load a sample of your real records, so you are looking at your own customers rather than a demo tenant full of invented ones.
